html:
The American Revolutionary War, from 1775 to 1783, was the war in which thirteen colonies of British North America won their independence from Britain and became the United States.

After the Seven Years' War, Britain taxed the colonies to pay its debts, and the colonists protested that they had no vote in Parliament. Fighting began at Lexington and Concord in April 1775. Congress made George Washington commander of the Continental Army and in July 1776 issued the Declaration of Independence.

  • Britain hired German soldiers, many from Hesse-Kassel, and held New York for most of the war.
  • The American win at Saratoga in 1777 brought France into the war in 1778, followed by Spain and the Dutch Republic, which led to the Fourth Anglo-Dutch War.
  • Washington and a French army and fleet trapped the main British army at Yorktown in 1781, which ended major fighting.
  • The Treaty of Paris of 1783 recognised the new nation.

The war split Native nations. The Haudenosaunee divided, and most Mohawk, Seneca and Cayuga fought for Britain and lost their lands. Tens of thousands of Loyalists left for Canada. Congress paid for the war with paper money that collapsed, and the Bank of North America was set up in 1781 to help. Losing America also pushed Britain to send convicts to Australia instead, through the First Fleet of 1788. France's debts from the war helped bring on the French Revolution.
sum: The American Revolutionary War, from 1775 to 1783, was the war in which thirteen colonies of British North America won their independence from Britain and became the United States.
